A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IDM-based semi-supervised imitation learning study. Their text, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable, and moved sections and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original maze/grid experiments and evaluations on 16 Procgen environments, Push-T and LIBERO-10 in Figures 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds a stochastic-environment maze experiment in Appendix D.1.4 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The LAPO+ stages, model architectures and UVA sampling procedures are retained. The reorganized LAPO descriptions, revised notation and new summary table do not establish a different algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: v2 adds a stochastic variant of the existing 50×50 maze, where actions can leave the agent stationary despite a deterministic expert. This extends environmental conditions beyond the earlier deterministic-dynamics experiments; the other datasets and tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding Procgen and manipulation comparisons retain their comparator sets. Figure 8 extends the existing BC versus VM*-IDM comparison, using linear classifiers and MLPs, without introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: The added Figure 8 experiment evaluates no-op probabilities 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 across training fractions from 1/32 to 1. Appendix D.1.4 specifies exact marginalization over stationary and moving transitions before computing policy accuracy. Existing experimental settings are not reported as changed.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1.4 adds a controlled robustness analysis asking whether the IDM advantage survives stochastic transitions that make the ground-truth IDM nonlinear. It also tests the limiting case of certain no-ops. Earlier complexity, goal-conditioning and expert-stochasticity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and uncertainty-reporting practices remain: five seeds for maze complexity/goals, ten for expert stochasticity, and three for Procgen and manipulation. Figure 8 follows the existing five-seed practice. Revised plotted error-bar values and styling do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Existing maze curves receive small numerical updates: in Figure 3, BC's mean reward at p(right)=0.5 and train split 0.4 changes from 1.0 to approximately 0.9. New Figure 8 reports an IDM advantage with occasional no-ops and its disappearance when no-ops are certain. The Procgen and manipulation result plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 in v2 expands v1's Appendix B.2 CNN representation proof with a Cauchy–Schwarz bound and explicit uniqueness reasoning. Appendix D.1.4 adds stochastic-IDM and policy-mixture derivations, while Section 4 makes the sample-efficiency premise explicitly probabilistic. The central equivalence argument and KL bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 2 now states the advantage conditionally, when complexity and/or stochasticity is lower, and explicitly labels the expected occurrence of these conditions in practice as a hypothesis. The other principal contributions and abstract claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains why partial linearity can preserve the IDM advantage under stochastic dynamics and why that advantage disappears with certain no-ops. It also qualifies the illustrative role of analytically simple IDMs in realistic settings and softens some generalizations from the maze experiments. The main Discussion limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a link to the authors' experiment code. Appendix D.2.1 newly documents Procgen evaluation every 500 training steps, averaging returns over 64 episodes and retaining the maximum during training. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hou et al. (2026) for world-model terminology and Kalimeris et al. (2019) for SGD learning functions of increasing complexity. It removes the discussion and citation of Nair et al. (2017). These are limited updates to otherwise retained research positioning.

P1.justification: The LAPO background moves from Section 5.1 into new Section 2.3.3, and Section 5.1 is rewritten to clarify LAPO+. v2 adds an author contribution appendix, adjusts terminology and makes localized prose corrections. Most narrative structure and text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method-summary Table 1, environment illustrations in Figure 4 and stochastic-maze plots in Figure 8. Existing maze plots have reordered legends and lighter error bars; other figures receive caption adjustments and relocation. The overall document layout is retained.

improvement.justification: The stochastic-maze analysis adds useful evidence about the advantage's applicability and failure boundary. The expanded appendix proof, code link, evaluation disclosures and method-summary table improve mathematical transparency, reproducibility information and clarity. These are limited gains; the core methods and main benchmark conclusions remain stable.
